title: Christ, Covenant and Light of the Nations
english: He who is God and Lord has appeared among us, according to the Scriptures (Psalm 118:27), and through Him the flock of those who were wandering has been gathered in, as in a net, to the grace that comes through faith. For He was the expectation of the nations (Genesis 49:10), and through Him God the Father called those in mist and darkness to the light of the truth. And He made this plain to us a little earlier, saying: “I, the Lord God, have called You in righteousness, and I will hold Your hand and strengthen You; and I have given You as a covenant of the race, as a light of the nations, to open the eyes of the blind, to bring out of bonds those who are bound, and out of the prison house those who sit in deep darkness” (Isaiah 42:6-7).

For our Lord Jesus Christ has been appointed by God the Father as a covenant for the race according to the flesh, I mean those of Israel, to whom God promised long ago through one of the prophets, saying: “Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will accomplish for the house of Israel and for the house of Judah a new covenant, not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers” (Jeremiah 31:31-32). For the divine Moses was a minister of shadow and type, standing in the rank of a suppliant; but Christ, as Son and Lord, became the arbiter of a new covenant. I call it new because it reshapes man into the newness of a holy life, and through the Gospel way of life shows him to be an approved and true worshipper; for “God is Spirit,” it says, “and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth” (John 4:24).

So He has been appointed as a covenant of the race and as a light of the nations, to open the eyes of the blind and to bring out of bonds those who are bound. For Satan, the author of evil, darkened the hearts of the nations; for “they became futile in their reasonings, and claiming to be wise they became fools, and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed beasts, and of creeping things” (Romans 1:21-23).

But the true light (John 1:9), that is, Christ, rose for us as a spiritual morning star and as the sun of righteousness (Malachi 4:2); spreading the ray of the true knowledge of God, He scattered the darkness that the devil's deceit had brought down on those upon the earth, and He set free from their bonds those who were held fast, beyond escape, by the chains of their own sins. So, since those who of old served the creation rather than the Creator (Romans 1:25), who had darkness in their minds, who … the works of their own hands …
